Bayesian coverage model page

Source: R/page-bayesian.R
bayesian_ui.Rd

The Bayesian coverage model page, shared by the apps and used at national level and at admin level 1. It has one card of charts with a tab for each indicator the app lists (cd_cfg("bayes_indicators"), by default cd_bayes_indicators), the only ones the model takes; each tab plots the model's coverage estimates by year. A model takes minutes to fit, so the fit runs in a background worker (cd_bayes_fit_task()) and the chart shows its loader meanwhile. A fit starts only when its tab is shown, from the dataset's bayes_model_inputs(); the result is kept in the dataset (keep_bayes_model()) and read back with bayes_model_cached(), so it is fitted once for an admin level, indicator and denominator. While the model's packages are missing (cd_bayes_packages_missing()) the page shows a notice and fits nothing: inside DataSuite the notice has a button that asks it to install them, elsewhere it shows the R command to run.

Usage

bayesian_ui(id, i18n, label)

bayesian_server(id, cache, i18n, admin_level, active = reactive(TRUE))

Arguments

id

The module's id. A page's id is also its entry in the app's page registry.

i18n

The app's translator (a shiny.i18n translator), used for every label.

label

Not used.

cache

A reactive that returns the dataset, a CacheConnection.

admin_level

A string, not a reactive: the level the models are fitted at, "national" or "adminlevel_1" (admin level 1).

active

A reactive that is TRUE once the page has been opened with data loaded. The page does no work before that.

Value

bayesian_ui() returns the page's UI as Shiny tags. bayesian_server() returns a reactive that holds the key of the tab shown: an indicator's name, or "custom".

Details

The page has no filters of its own. Apps register it with bayesian_page_server(), which also starts the workers.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# a page of your own with the same charts: start the workers, then call the server.
# The id must be a page in the app's page registry.
my_bayes_ui <- function(id, i18n) bayesian_ui(id, i18n)
my_bayes_server <- function(id, cache, i18n, active = reactive(TRUE)) {
  cd_start_bayes_workers()
  bayesian_server(id, cache, i18n, "adminlevel_1", active = active)
}
} # }
